checks: Credential/header/key redaction is checked before any diagnostic can be retained.
Wrong password is refused; empty sign-in stays disabled and the passcode is cleared.
Browser visibility lifecycle covers the private DOM, waits for actual /v1/me, and restores the same mounted workspace.
A controlled foreground503 keeps private views covered; explicit retry rechecks the real service and restores the same DOM.
Separate worker prepares actual PDF/CSV; browser saves and parses protected artifacts at the current report revision.
Top Sign out closes private views and revokes the session while foreground access checking is stalled.
A real server-side account disablement closes private views on resume; a fresh login works after independent reactivation.
An independently disabled account is refused despite a correct passcode.
Client expiry uses setSystemTime plus a short timer advance and closes private views without replaying hours of intervals.
All four preauthorised roles pass at 320px and 390px; logout revokes each opaque server session.
Thirteen named profiles, four accepted fixtures and two completed games agree with manager/player screens.

Past game cards at both phone widths omit every availability action while retaining exact recorded replies and attendance; upcoming unplayed games keep their reply actions, and period navigation causes no POST or service preparation change.
Generated passwords and login tokens are absent from built assets, visible workspace text and browser journal/preferences.
Administrator club save preserves the separate unsaved Team name draft across accepted refresh without submitting it.

Actual concurrent administrator update produces the existing COMMAND_REJECTED422; the editor retains editable drafts with no automatic POST, and explicit refresh exposes the latest value for separate keep-draft review.
Controlled required configuration503 retains the same disabled draft and explicit retry restores it; configuration403 closes private views even while independently verified /v1/me remains200.

One separately labelled filtered-records GET projection marks a same-day game completed while its actual canonical match remains unstarted; Home omits its reply and Schedule hides all reply actions, preserves recorded details, leaves another unplayed game open, and restores the actual records without any preparation write.
Player upcoming RSVP is accepted without changing actual attendance or manager selection; accepted refresh retains the same match card, Matches filter and usable Schedule.

Actual concurrent profile-field change rejects a stale full-form save; explicit refresh retains the draft but blocks saving at its original revision, and discard/reopen reveals the newer saved field without publishing the unsaved name.
Two actual fixture reply mutations retain the selected Schedule detail through accepted refresh, allowing the next player edit.

The first actual Manager kickoff recovers from its newer event anchor, shows a numeric substitution countdown, decreases during active play and leaves the confirmed lineup/revision/outbox unchanged; speaker delivery remains a separate hardware check.

Manager explicitly claims recording, checks in nine players, stages seven eligible places, confirms kickoff and referee pause, navigates back/return, and uploads; independent HTTP verifies accepted attendance, lineup and clock.

After actual future profile/template edits, Schedule reopens the saved recorded match without preparation POST or immutable-history failure; its original squad/formation and accepted clock remain unchanged.
A selected player archived through an actual manager command remains visible in the future fixture until explicit UI removal; accepted selection changes without inferred attendance.

Future occurrence and reviewed series drafts expose archived expected players for explicit removal and save successfully; future attendance and complete held/cancelled records remain unchanged, with archived historical attendance visible and read-only.

An open penalty draft survives a clock-resume upload with its captured time; local goal stays invisible to spectators until explicit upload, then actual accepted polling updates a second browser automatically. This is functional loopback evidence, not a network latency benchmark.
Actual Roma manager grant revocation closes its private workspace on foreground even while /v1/me200 retains a separate Milan manager grant; the exact temporary membership changes are then restored.
